# The Strong Maximal Rank Conjecture

18 years old · traced to 2008

Let $g,r,d,k$g,r,d,k satisfy

$$g-d+r\geq0,\qquad 0\leq\rho(g,r,d)<r-2,\qquad k\geq2,$$g−d+r≥0,0≤ρ(g,r,d)<r−2,k≥2,

and let $C$C be a general curve of genus $g$g. For $L\in W^r_dC$L∈W d r​C, define the multiplication map

$$\phi^k_L:\operatorname{Sym}^k H^0(C,L)\longrightarrow H^0(C,L^{\otimes k}).$$ϕ L k​:Sym k H 0(C,L)⟶H 0(C,L⊗k).

The Strong Maximal Rank Conjecture. The locus of line bundles $L\in W^r_dC$L∈W d r​C for which $\phi^k_L$ϕ L k​ is not of maximal rank has dimension

$$\rho(g,r,d)-1-\left|{r+k\choose k}-(dk+1-g)\right|.$$ρ(g,r,d)−1−​(k r+k​)−(d k+1−g)​.

In particular, $\phi^k_L$ϕ L k​ is of maximal rank for every $L\in W^r_dC$L∈W d r​C when this quantity is negative.

This strengthens the Maximal Rank Conjecture by predicting the dimension of the exceptional locus of linear series on a general curve. The conjecture remains open in general, although the supplied status evidence says that recent tropical methods prove three cases.

References

2 papers in this index state this conjecture (2008–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are arXiv:0811.3117.

Source: Isabel Vogt, “Recent advances in Brill–Noether theory and the geometry of Brill–Noether curves”, arXiv:2602.03660 (2026).

Title: The Stratified and the Strong Maximal Rank Conjecture in $\mathbb{P}^3$ and $\mathbb{P}^4$
Authors: Vlad Robu
Date: Sat May 23 14:50:42 2026

We prove that the Strong Maximal Rank Conjecture holds for quadrics in $\mathbb{P}^3$ and we prove the existence of a component of the expected dimension in $\mathbb{P}^4$, as well as in a wide range of parameters $(g,d)$ in $\mathbb{P}^r$ with $r\ge 5$. We propose the Stratified Strong Maximal Rank Conjecture which also takes into account the rank $k$ of quadrics and prove it works in most of the cases when $k=3$ and $k=4$. We also prove a partial result that concerns the unrepresentability of the canonical bundle of a general curve as a sum of $3$ pencils.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We show that the ball does not maximize the ﬁrst nonzero 
Steklov eigenvalue among all contractible domains of ﬁxed 
boundary volume in Rn when n ≥3. This is in contrast to 
the situation when n = 2, where a result of Weinstock from 
1954 shows that the disk uniquely maximizes the ﬁrst Steklov 
eigenvalue among all simply connected domains in the plane 
having the same boundary length. When n ≥3, we show 
that increasing the number of boundary components does not 
increase the normalized (by boundary volume) ﬁrst Steklov 
eigenvalue. This is in contrast to recent results which have 
been obtained for surfaces and for convex domains.

By a conformal blow-up at any boundary point \(p\in\partial\Sigma\), we have the following sharp area lower bound for free boundary minimal surfaces in \(\mathbb{B}^n\). Note that \(2|\Sigma|=|\partial\Sigma|\) by Proposition 2.4.

**Theorem 7.2** (Fraser-Schoen [24]). Let \(\Sigma^2\) be an immersed free boundary minimal surface in \(\mathbb{B}^n\). Then,

\[
|\Sigma^2|\ge |\mathbb{B}^2|=\pi
\]

and equality holds if and only if \(\Sigma^2\) is an equatorial plane disk.

By a direct monotonicity-type argument, Brendle was able to generalize Fraser and Schoen’s result to any dimension and codimension.

**Theorem 7.3** (Brendle [5]). Let \(\Sigma^k\) be an immersed free boundary minimal submanifold in \(\mathbb{B}^n\). Then,

\[
|\Sigma^k|\ge |\mathbb{B}^k|
\]

and equality holds if and only if \(\Sigma^k\) is congruent to \(\mathbb{B}^k\).

Note that the sharp area bounds above imply the sharp isoperimetric inequality for free boundary minimal submanifolds in \(\mathbb{B}^n\) (see [24, Corollary 5.5] and [5, Corollary 5]). Motivated by Theorem 7.1, Fraser and Schoen conjectured that the same statement hold in arbitrary dimension and codimension.

**Open Question 9.** Let \(\Sigma^k\) be an immersed free boundary minimal submanifold in \(\mathbb{B}^n\). Suppose \(f:\mathbb{B}^n\to\mathbb{B}^n\) is a conformal diffeomorphism. Is it true that \(|f(\partial\Sigma)|\le |\partial\Sigma|?\)

Note that an affirmative answer to **Open Question 9** would imply Theorem 7.3. When \(\Sigma\) is a cone, it follows from the corresponding results of Li-Yau and El Soufi-Ilias applied to its link in \(\mathbb{S}^{n-1}\). # Minimal surfaces and eigenvalue problems

Aliana Fraser and Richard Schoen

**Abstract.** We show that metrics that maximize the k-th Steklov eigenvalue on surfaces with boundary arise from free boundary minimal surfaces in the unit ball. We prove several properties of the volumes of these minimal submanifolds. For free boundary minimal submanifolds in the ball we show that the boundary volume is reduced up to second order under conformal transformations of the ball. For two-dimensional stationary integer multiplicity rectifiable varifolds that are stationary for deformations that preserve the ball, we prove that the boundary length is reduced under conformal transformations. We also give an overview of some of the known results on extremal metrics of the Laplacian on closed surfaces, and give a survey of our recent results from Fraser and Schoen (2012) on extremal metrics for Steklov eigenvalues on compact surfaces with boundary.
